quiescence_checks.source: board advisory claims; claims dict keyed by resource with session_id and expires_at; the messages list beside it is not claims
quiescence_checks.children_definition: distinct non-predecessor sessions holding unexpired claims under a resource prefix
quiescence_checks.expiry: board filters expired claims itself (verified); checks re-filter defensively
quiescence_checks.fail_open_hole_fixed: coordinator read CLAIMS_CMD output but not exit status; empty output means none held, so an erroring check cleared the gate
quiescence_checks.standing_of_the_board_check: claim-backed and CONDITIONAL on complete child registration: it establishes 'no unexpired claim is held', not 'no child is running'. A child that never registered, released early, or let its claim lapse is invisible to it.

second_independent_check.source: the OS process tree; needs no registration at all
second_independent_check.semantics: an UPPER BOUND on live child sessions -- one child can show as several processes, because a Codex launch is `node /usr/bin/codex` plus the vendored native binary it execs, and bash briefly forks a subshell carrying its parent's argv. The gate is == 0, so over-counting only blocks a rotation.
second_independent_check.fail_open_found_and_removed: an earlier version collapsed a matching parent/child pair sharing a CLI name into 'one session' to avoid double-counting the Codex pair. A claude root that spawned a claude child is exactly that shape, so a live child would have been counted as zero -- the one direction a quiescence gate must not have. Removed in favour of the upper bound.
second_independent_check.unlocatable_root: exit 32 (not established): 'I could not find the root' is not 'the root has no children'
second_independent_check.validated_against_a_real_root: the live idle Claude root in the rootlive3 server returns 0; its only child process is an MCP server, which correctly does not match the session pattern, so the check does not block live rotations
second_independent_check.what_still_evades_both: a detached child (setsid/nohup) or a turn queued into a session hosted elsewhere

quiescence_checks.coverage_claim: neither check is a completeness basis on its own; a child must evade BOTH to pass unseen

registration_is_not_merely_incomplete.observed_2026-10-24: the live board returns 0 active claims; 56 claims are stored and expired ones are never removed
registration_is_not_merely_incomplete.consequence: the board-backed children check returns 0 on every rotation, so in current practice it has no discriminating power at all. Its standing is weaker than 'conditional on complete registration': no session is registering. Quiescence therefore rests on the descendant check, which needs no registration.
registration_is_not_merely_incomplete.source: an independent review of board usage, confirmed here by querying the live board directly
registration_is_not_merely_incomplete.implication: the claims check should be treated as a second signal that is currently silent, not as evidence of quiescence. It is kept because it is the only check that can see a child on another host.

triggerable_rotation.authority: GATE_AUTHORITY allowlist of authors/session ids; APPROVE_TOKEN in the body; unset allowlist refuses to run (exit 77)
triggerable_rotation.audit: authorized-by and last-rejected-trigger record the message ids
triggerable_rotation.verified: unauthorized author carrying the correct token ignored and recorded, watch re-armed, authorized approval then committed
triggerable_rotation.doctrine_question: whether a board message may carry root-transfer authority is the skill owner's call; board claims are stamped advisory_coordination_only
triggerable_rotation.artifact_binding: the approval body must carry the handoff's sha256. Author + token alone approves 'a rotation', not 'this handoff', so a stale or replayed approval would commit whatever the watch was started with. Three outcomes are distinguished and recorded: APPROVED, UNAUTHORIZED (named approver missing), UNBOUND (digest missing or for another artifact).
triggerable_rotation.binding_limits: binds to CONTENT, not to a generation: two rotations of a byte-identical handoff share a digest. The board identifies authors; it does not authenticate them, so the allowlist is identification only. A lease/generation guard for the board-cursor TOCTOU is still NOT built.
triggerable_rotation.verified_binding: approval with token but no digest -> ignored and recorded as unbound; approval citing another digest -> ignored; unauthorized author carrying BOTH a valid token and the correct digest -> ignored and recorded; correctly bound approval from a named approver -> committed
